items.rule: Make every video its own work: its own script, pictures and structure. Never a fill-in template with only the names changed.
items.why: YouTube does not pay for templated or mass-produced content, and it judges the whole channel.
items.check: Compare with the channel's other videos: different script, different pictures, different structure.

items.rule: No AI character presents as a doctor, lawyer or money expert giving advice.
items.why: YouTube does not pay for AI personas giving health, legal or finance advice.
items.check: Read the script: characters share ideas and sources, never personal advice.

items.rule: Summarize the book's ideas in your own words, keep quotes short, and credit the book and author on screen.
items.why: A recap that replaces the book, or long excerpts, is high copyright risk.
items.check: Transcript has no long quotes; the book and author are named on screen.

items.rule: Turn on YouTube's AI label only when the video looks realistic. Clearly animated videos do not need it.
items.why: Only realistic synthetic content needs the label.
items.check: Animated style: no label needed. Realistic people or places: label on.

items.rule: Offer anything in return for likes, subscribes or comments.
items.why: Asking is allowed; rewarding engagement is not.
items.check: Transcript and screen: no 'like to win', no prizes for subscribing.

items.rule: Open on the promise or payoff in the first seconds. No greeting, no slow intro.
items.why: The share still watching at 30 seconds (Intros) is the first thing that drops; YouTube rewards satisfied viewers.
items.check: Frame at 0 s shows the subject; the first sentence states what the viewer gets.

items.rule: Say or show the book's name in the first 15 seconds.
items.why: Top book summary titles lead with the book; viewers should know at once they are in the right place.
items.check: The book title is on screen or spoken by 15 s.

items.rule: Use a clear structure: numbered takeaways with a section card for each.
items.why: Structured videos kept more viewers than talking-head videos in one 2026 channel study.

items.rule: For a full book summary, plan 30 to 50 minutes in one video.
items.why: The top book summary channel runs about 49 minutes; long videos also build the 8,000 watch hours needed from 2027.
items.check: duration_s of the full video is 1,800 or more.

items.rule: Keep one book in one video. Do not split it into parts.
items.why: A 'Part 2' drew far fewer views on the top channel.
items.check: No 'Part 1/Part 2' in the title or script.

items.rule: End with a 5 to 20 second end screen that points to the next video, with room for up to 4 elements.
items.why: End screens only run in the last 5 to 20 seconds; suggested videos are where most viewing comes from.
items.check: The last 5 seconds or more are an end card with free space for video links.

items.rule: Make it a series: name what comes next and link it.
items.why: Viewers mostly find videos through suggested videos, not the subscription feed.
items.check: The video names the next video or takeaway.

items.rule: Title: the exact book title plus a time promise (for example 'Atomic Habits in 30 Minutes').
items.why: This is the title pattern of the top book summary channel.

items.rule: Thumbnail: a face (a character face counts as a face here) and about 5 words or fewer.
items.why: Most breakout thumbnails in a 500-video 2026 study had a face; the median text was 5 words.

items.rule: Test up to 3 titles and thumbnails with YouTube's A/B test.
items.why: YouTube picks the winner by watch time.
items.check: Test set up in YouTube Studio.

items.rule: Use the same format and visuals video after video until it feels repetitive.
items.why: A big psychology channel's views fell with repetitive listicles; templated channels are not paid.
items.check: Compare with the channel's last videos.

items.why: The top book summary channel grew to 307K subscribers with 20 videos.

items.rule: Add chapters for videos over 5 minutes (first at 0:00, at least 3).
items.why: Chapters need 0:00 and 3 timestamps to show.

gaps: No dated 2026 source on how often the picture should change in explainer videos (pacing). Not scored.
No US-only data: most studies are global.
No 2026 source on narration voice or music choice for book summaries.
No YouTube Data API key yet, so no list of the top book summary videos of the last 12 months with exact counts.
TikTok, Reels and Shorts were not researched in this run (the test video is 16:9 long-form).
